metadata.title: Score-Based Generative Modeling through Stochastic Differential Equations
metadata.authors: Yang Song, Jascha Sohl-Dickstein, Diederik P. Kingma, Abhishek Kumar, Stefano Ermon, Ben Poole

nodes.name: Score (gradient of log-density)
nodes.statement: The $\emph{score}$ of a distribution $p(\bfx)$ is the gradient of its log-density with respect to data, $\nabla_\bfx \log p(\bfx)$.
nodes.statement_clean: The score is the gradient of the log probability density with respect to the data.

nodes.name: Perturbation kernel and perturbed data distribution (SMLD)
nodes.statement: $p_{\sigma}(\tilde{\bfx} \mid \bfx) \coloneqq \mcal{N}(\tilde{\bfx}; \bfx, \sigma^2 \bfI)$ and $p_{\sigma}(\tilde{\bfx}) \coloneqq \int p_\text{data}(\bfx) p_{\sigma}(\tilde{\bfx} \mid \bfx)\,\ud \bfx$, with noise scales $\sm = \sigma_1 < \cdots < \sigma_N = \sM$.

nodes.name: Noise Conditional Score Network (NCSN)
nodes.statement: A neural network $\bfs_\bftheta(\bfx, \sigma)$ trained to approximate $\nabla_\bfx \log p_{\sigma}(\bfx)$ at every noise scale $\sigma$.

nodes.name: DDPM forward Markov chain and perturbation kernel
nodes.statement: Discrete Markov chain $p(\bfx_i \mid \bfx_{i-1}) = \mcal{N}(\bfx_i; \sqrt{1-\beta_i}\,\bfx_{i-1}, \beta_i \bfI)$ with $\alpha_i := \prod_{j=1}^{i}(1-\beta_j)$, giving $p_{\alpha_i}(\bfx_i \mid \bfx_0) = \mcal{N}(\bfx_i; \sqrt{\alpha_i}\,\bfx_0, (1-\alpha_i)\bfI)$.
nodes.origin_citation: Sohl-Dickstein et al. 2015; Ho et al. 2020

nodes.name: Forward Itô SDE for diffusion process
nodes.statement: $\ud \bfx = \bff(\bfx, t)\, \ud t + g(t)\, \ud \bfw$, where $\bfw$ is a standard Wiener process, $\bff(\cdot, t)$ is the drift coefficient, and $g(t)$ is the diffusion coefficient.

nodes.name: Reverse-time SDE
nodes.section: 3.2 Generating samples by reversing the SDE
nodes.statement: $\ud \bfx = [\bff(\bfx, t) - g(t)^2 \nabla_\bfx \log p_t(\bfx)]\, \ud t + g(t)\, \ud \bar{\bfw}$, where $\bar{\bfw}$ is a Wiener process running backward in time.

nodes.name: Variance Exploding (VE) SDE
nodes.statement: $\ud \bfx = \sqrt{\frac{\ud[\sigma^2(t)]}{\ud t}}\, \ud \bfw$. The continuous-time limit of the SMLD perturbation Markov chain; its variance diverges as $t \to \infty$.

nodes.name: Variance Preserving (VP) SDE
nodes.statement: $\ud \bfx = -\tfrac{1}{2}\beta(t)\bfx\, \ud t + \sqrt{\beta(t)}\, \ud \bfw$. The continuous-time limit of the DDPM Markov chain; preserves unit variance when started from unit-variance data.

nodes.name: sub-VP SDE
nodes.statement: $\ud \bfx = -\tfrac{1}{2}\beta(t)\bfx\, \ud t + \sqrt{\beta(t)(1 - e^{-2\int_0^t \beta(s)\ud s})}\, \ud \bfw$. A new SDE whose variance is upper-bounded by the corresponding VP SDE at every $t$.

nodes.name: Probability flow ODE
nodes.statement: $\ud \bfx = [\bff(\bfx, t) - \tfrac{1}{2} g(t)^2 \nabla_\bfx \log p_t(\bfx)]\, \ud t$. A deterministic ODE whose marginals match those of the forward SDE.

nodes.name: General matrix-diffusion SDE
nodes.statement: $\ud \bfx = \bff(\bfx, t)\, \ud t + \bfG(\bfx, t)\, \ud \bfw$ with $\bfG: \mbb{R}^d \to \mbb{R}^{d\times d}$, with reverse-time form $\ud \bfx = \{\bff - \nabla\cdot[\bfG\bfG\tran] - \bfG\bfG\tran \nabla_\bfx \log p_t(\bfx)\}\, \ud t + \bfG\, \ud \bar{\bfw}$.

nodes.name: Conditional reverse-time SDE
nodes.statement: $\ud \bfx = \{\bff(\bfx, t) - g(t)^2[\nabla_\bfx \log p_t(\bfx) + \nabla_\bfx \log p_t(\bfy \mid \bfx)]\}\, \ud t + g(t)\, \ud \bar{\bfw}$, sampling from $p_0(\bfx \mid \bfy)$.

nodes.name: SMLD denoising score-matching objective
nodes.statement: $\bftheta^* = \argmin_\bftheta \sum_{i=1}^N \sigma_i^2\, \mbb{E}_{p_\text{data}(\bfx)} \mbb{E}_{p_{\sigma_i}(\tilde{\bfx}\mid\bfx)} \big[\norm{\bfs_\bftheta(\tilde{\bfx}, \sigma_i) - \nabla_{\tilde{\bfx}}\log p_{\sigma_i}(\tilde{\bfx}\mid\bfx)}_2^2\big]$.

nodes.name: DDPM re-weighted ELBO objective
nodes.statement: $\bftheta^* = \argmin_\bftheta \sum_{i=1}^N (1-\alpha_i)\, \mbb{E}_{p_\text{data}}\mbb{E}_{p_{\alpha_i}(\tilde{\bfx}\mid\bfx)} [\norm{\bfs_\bftheta(\tilde{\bfx}, i) - \nabla_{\tilde{\bfx}}\log p_{\alpha_i}(\tilde{\bfx}\mid\bfx)}_2^2]$ ($L_\text{simple}$ rewritten as denoising score matching).

nodes.name: Continuous-time score-matching training objective
nodes.statement: $\bftheta^* = \argmin_\bftheta \mbb{E}_t\{\lambda(t)\, \mbb{E}_{\bfx(0)}\mbb{E}_{\bfx(t)\mid\bfx(0)} [\norm{\bfs_\bftheta(\bfx(t), t) - \nabla_{\bfx(t)}\log p_{0t}(\bfx(t)\mid\bfx(0))}_2^2]\}$, with $t \sim \mcal{U}(0, T)$ and weight $\lambda(t) > 0$.

nodes.name: Sliced-score-matching variant of the training objective
nodes.statement: $\bftheta^* = \argmin_\bftheta \mbb{E}_t\{\lambda(t)\,\mbb{E}_{\bfx(0)}\mbb{E}_{\bfx(t)}\mbb{E}_{\bfv\sim p_\bfv}[\tfrac{1}{2}\norm{\bfs_\bftheta(\bfx(t), t)}_2^2 + \bfv\tran \bfs_\bftheta(\bfx(t), t)\bfv]\}$ for non-affine drifts where the transition kernel is intractable.

nodes.name: Closed-form Gaussian perturbation kernels for VE/VP/sub-VP
nodes.statement: $p_{0t}(\bfx(t)\mid\bfx(0))$ is Gaussian with explicit mean and covariance for each of the VE, VP, and sub-VP SDEs (Eq.~(perturb_kernel)).

nodes.name: Skilling-Hutchinson trace estimator for log-likelihood divergence
nodes.statement: $\nabla \cdot \tilde{\bff}_\bftheta(\bfx, t) = \mbb{E}_{p(\bfe)}[\bfe\tran \nabla \tilde{\bff}_\bftheta(\bfx, t)\, \bfe]$ with $\mbb{E}[\bfe] = \bfzero$, $\operatorname{Cov}[\bfe] = \bfI$.

nodes.name: Anderson's reverse-time SDE
nodes.section: 3.2 Generating samples by reversing the SDE
nodes.statement: The reverse of the diffusion process $\ud \bfx = \bff(\bfx, t)\, \ud t + g(t)\, \ud \bfw$ is itself a diffusion, satisfying $\ud \bfx = [\bff(\bfx, t) - g(t)^2 \nabla_\bfx \log p_t(\bfx)]\, \ud t + g(t)\, \ud \bar{\bfw}$.
assumptions: $\bfx(t)$ solves the forward SDE $\ud \bfx = \bff(\bfx, t)\, \ud t + g(t)\, \ud \bfw$
Coefficients $\bff, g$ are sufficiently regular for a unique strong solution
conclusions: There exists a reverse-time diffusion equal in law (running $t: T \to 0$) to the forward process whose drift involves the score $\nabla_\bfx \log p_t(\bfx)$

nodes.name: Probability flow ODE matches SDE marginals
nodes.statement: For the forward SDE in $\ud\bfx = \bff\, \ud t + \bfG\, \ud \bfw$, the deterministic ODE $\ud \bfx = \{\bff - \tfrac{1}{2}\nabla\cdot[\bfG\bfG\tran] - \tfrac{1}{2}\bfG\bfG\tran \nabla_\bfx \log p_t(\bfx)\}\, \ud t$ induces the same time-marginal densities $\{p_t(\bfx)\}_{t=0}^T$ as the SDE.
assumptions: Score $\nabla_\bfx \log p_t(\bfx)$ is well-defined for all $t$
conclusions: The probability flow ODE has the same marginal densities $p_t(\bfx)$ as the forward SDE for all $t \in [0, T]$

nodes.name: Variance bound: sub-VP $\preccurlyeq$ VP
nodes.statement: For the sub-VP and VP SDEs sharing $\beta(s)$ and initial covariance $\bfsigma(0)$: $\bfsigma_\text{sub-VP}(t) \preccurlyeq \bfsigma_\text{VP}(t)$ for all $t \geq 0$, and both converge to $\bfI$ as $t \to \infty$ provided $\int_0^\infty \beta(s)\, \ud s = \infty$.

nodes.name: Conditional reverse-time SDE for posterior sampling
nodes.statement: Given the forward SDE and a known forward likelihood $p_t(\bfy \mid \bfx(t))$, the process $p_0(\bfx \mid \bfy)$ is sampled by the conditional reverse-time SDE $\ud \bfx = \{\bff - g^2[\nabla_\bfx \log p_t(\bfx) + \nabla_\bfx \log p_t(\bfy \mid \bfx)]\}\, \ud t + g\, \ud \bar{\bfw}$.
assumptions: $\bfx(t)$ solves the forward SDE in $\ud\bfx = \bff\, \ud t + g\, \ud \bfw$
$\nabla_\bfx \log p_t(\bfy \mid \bfx)$ is available (from auxiliary model or estimator)
conclusions: Solving the conditional reverse-time SDE from $\bfx(T) \sim p_T(\bfx \mid \bfy)$ produces samples $\bfx(0) \sim p_0(\bfx \mid \bfy)$

nodes.name: Closed-form transition kernel for affine drift
nodes.statement: When $\bff(\cdot, t)$ is affine, the transition kernel $p_{0t}(\bfx(t) \mid \bfx(0))$ is Gaussian with mean and covariance computable in closed form via standard linear-SDE techniques.
assumptions: The drift $\bff(\cdot, t)$ is affine in $\bfx$
conclusions: $p_{0t}(\bfx(t)\mid\bfx(0))$ is Gaussian with closed-form mean and covariance

nodes.name: Reverse-diffusion sampler matches DDPM ancestral sampler in the limit
nodes.statement: The DDPM ancestral sampling rule (Eq.~\eqref{eqn:ddpm_sampling}) is recovered from the reverse-diffusion discretization \eqref{eqn:discrete_backward} of the reverse-time VP SDE in the limit $\beta_i \to 0$, i.e.\ both reduce to the same continuous-time reverse SDE.
conclusions: Ancestral sampling and reverse-diffusion sampling correspond to two consistent discretizations of the same reverse-time VP SDE

nodes.name: Proof of probability flow ODE marginal equivalence
nodes.statement: Manipulate the Fokker-Planck equation for $p_t$ to express it as a continuity equation with effective drift $\tilde{\bff} = \bff - \tfrac{1}{2}\nabla\cdot[\bfG\bfG\tran] - \tfrac{1}{2}\bfG\bfG\tran \nabla_\bfx \log p_t$, which is the Liouville equation of the corresponding ODE.

nodes.name: Write Fokker-Planck (Kolmogorov forward) equation
nodes.statement: Express $\partial_t p_t(\bfx) = -\sum_i \partial_{x_i}[f_i p_t] + \tfrac{1}{2}\sum_{i,j}\partial^2_{x_ix_j}[\sum_k G_{ik}G_{jk} p_t]$.

nodes.name: Refactor second-order term using $\nabla_\bfx \log p_t$
nodes.statement: Use $\partial_{x_j}[\cdot p_t] = (\partial_{x_j}\cdot)p_t + (\partial_{x_j}\log p_t) \cdot p_t$ to rewrite the diffusion term as $p_t \nabla\cdot[\bfG\bfG\tran] + p_t \bfG\bfG\tran \nabla_\bfx \log p_t$.

nodes.name: Combine into a continuity equation
nodes.statement: Collapse the equation into $\partial_t p_t = -\sum_i \partial_{x_i}[\tilde{f}_i p_t]$ with $\tilde{\bff} := \bff - \tfrac{1}{2}\nabla\cdot[\bfG\bfG\tran] - \tfrac{1}{2}\bfG\bfG\tran \nabla_\bfx \log p_t$.

nodes.name: Identify with Liouville equation of ODE
nodes.statement: The continuity equation is Kolmogorov's forward equation of the ODE $\ud\bfx = \tilde{\bff}(\bfx, t)\, \ud t$ (zero diffusion), so this ODE has the same marginals $p_t$ as the original SDE.

nodes.name: Derivation of VE SDE as continuum limit of SMLD chain
nodes.statement: Identify $\sigma(i/N) = \sigma_i$ in the SMLD update, take $\Delta t = 1/N$, expand $\sqrt{\sigma^2(t+\Delta t) - \sigma^2(t)} \approx \sqrt{(\ud[\sigma^2]/\ud t)\,\Delta t}$, and let $\Delta t \to 0$.

nodes.name: Re-index the SMLD Markov chain in continuous time
nodes.statement: Let $\bfx(i/N) = \bfx_i$, $\sigma(i/N) = \sigma_i$, $\bfz(i/N) = \bfz_i$, with $\Delta t = 1/N$ and $t \in \{0, 1/N, \ldots, (N-1)/N\}$.

nodes.name: Taylor-expand the noise increment
nodes.statement: $\bfx(t+\Delta t) = \bfx(t) + \sqrt{\sigma^2(t+\Delta t) - \sigma^2(t)}\,\bfz(t) \approx \bfx(t) + \sqrt{(\ud[\sigma^2(t)]/\ud t)\,\Delta t}\,\bfz(t)$ for $\Delta t \ll 1$.

nodes.name: Take $\Delta t \to 0$ limit
nodes.statement: The discrete update converges to $\ud \bfx = \sqrt{\ud[\sigma^2(t)]/\ud t}\, \ud \bfw$, the VE SDE.

nodes.name: Derivation of VP SDE as continuum limit of DDPM chain
nodes.statement: Re-parameterize $\bbeta_i = N\beta_i$, identify $\beta(i/N) = \bbeta_i$, expand $\sqrt{1 - \beta(t+\Delta t)\Delta t} \approx 1 - \tfrac{1}{2}\beta(t)\Delta t$, and let $\Delta t \to 0$.

nodes.name: Re-scale $\beta_i$ to keep finite limit
nodes.statement: Define $\bbeta_i = N \beta_i$ so that $\bfx_i = \sqrt{1 - \bbeta_i/N}\,\bfx_{i-1} + \sqrt{\bbeta_i/N}\,\bfz_{i-1}$.

nodes.name: Continuous-time reindexing
nodes.statement: Let $\beta(i/N) = \bbeta_i$, $\bfx(i/N) = \bfx_i$, $\bfz(i/N) = \bfz_i$, with $\Delta t = 1/N$.

nodes.name: Taylor-expand the rescaling factor
nodes.statement: $\bfx(t+\Delta t) \approx \bfx(t) - \tfrac{1}{2}\beta(t)\Delta t\,\bfx(t) + \sqrt{\beta(t)\Delta t}\,\bfz(t)$ for $\Delta t \ll 1$.

nodes.name: Take $\Delta t \to 0$ limit
nodes.statement: The chain converges to $\ud \bfx = -\tfrac{1}{2}\beta(t)\bfx\, \ud t + \sqrt{\beta(t)}\, \ud \bfw$, the VP SDE.

nodes.name: Proof of variance bound $\bfsigma_\text{sub-VP} \preccurlyeq \bfsigma_\text{VP}$
nodes.statement: Solve the ODE for $\bfsigma(t)$ (Eq.~5.51 in Särkkä) for both VP and sub-VP SDEs and compare term-by-term.

nodes.name: Derive variance ODE for VP
nodes.statement: Use Särkkä Eq.~(5.51) for affine SDEs to obtain $\ud\bfsigma_\text{VP}/\ud t = \beta(t)(\bfI - \bfsigma_\text{VP}(t))$.

nodes.name: Solve VP variance ODE in closed form
nodes.statement: $\bfsigma_\text{VP}(t) = \bfI + e^{-\int_0^t \beta(s)\,\ud s}(\bfsigma_\text{VP}(0) - \bfI)$.

nodes.name: Solve sub-VP variance
nodes.statement: $\bfsigma_\text{sub-VP}(t) = \bfI + e^{-2\int_0^t \beta(s)\,\ud s}\bfI + e^{-\int_0^t \beta(s)\,\ud s}(\bfsigma_\text{sub-VP}(0) - 2\bfI)$.

nodes.name: Compare and conclude
nodes.statement: With shared $\beta(s)$ and $\bfsigma(0)$, term-by-term inspection yields $\bfsigma_\text{sub-VP}(t) \preccurlyeq \bfsigma_\text{VP}(t)$, and both tend to $\bfI$ as $t \to \infty$ when $\int_0^\infty \beta(s)\,\ud s = \infty$.

nodes.name: Proof that ancestral sampling matches reverse-diffusion sampling
nodes.statement: Substitute $1/\sqrt{1-\beta_{i+1}} = 1 + \tfrac{1}{2}\beta_{i+1} + o(\beta_{i+1})$ into the DDPM ancestral update; drop $O(\beta_{i+1}^2)$ terms; identify the resulting form with the reverse-diffusion discretization of the reverse-time VP SDE.

nodes.name: Substitute into DDPM ancestral update
nodes.statement: $\bfx_i = (1 + \tfrac{1}{2}\beta_{i+1})(\bfx_{i+1} + \beta_{i+1}\bfs_{\bftheta^*}) + \sqrt{\beta_{i+1}}\bfz_{i+1}$ up to $o(\beta_{i+1})$.

nodes.name: Drop second-order $\beta_{i+1}^2$ terms
nodes.statement: Keep only $O(\beta_{i+1})$ terms: $\bfx_i \approx (2 - \sqrt{1 - \beta_{i+1}})\bfx_{i+1} + \beta_{i+1}\bfs_{\bftheta^*} + \sqrt{\beta_{i+1}}\bfz_{i+1}$.

nodes.name: Identify with reverse-diffusion discretization
nodes.statement: The result matches \eqref{eqn:discrete_backward} for the VP SDE, so DDPM ancestral sampling is a discretization of the same reverse-time VP SDE.

nodes.name: Predictor-Corrector (PC) sampler (general)
nodes.statement: Iterative reverse-time SDE sampler that alternates between a predictor (numerical SDE solver step) and a corrector (score-based MCMC step) at each discretization level.
input: Number of discretization steps $N$ for the reverse-time SDE
Number of corrector steps $M$ per noise level
nodes.pseudocode: Initialize $\bfx_N \sim p_T$; for $i = N-1$ down to $0$: $\bfx_i \gets \operatorname{Predictor}(\bfx_{i+1})$; for $j = 1$ to $M$: $\bfx_i \gets \operatorname{Corrector}(\bfx_i)$; return $\bfx_0$.

nodes.name: Initialize from prior
nodes.statement: $\bfx_N \sim p_T(\bfx)$.

nodes.name: Outer loop over reverse-time discretization
nodes.statement: For $i = N-1$ down to $0$, run a predictor step then $M$ corrector steps.

nodes.name: Predictor step
nodes.statement: $\bfx_i \gets \operatorname{Predictor}(\bfx_{i+1})$ using a numerical SDE solver (e.g.\ reverse-diffusion or ancestral) for the reverse-time SDE.

nodes.name: Inner corrector loop
nodes.statement: For $j = 1$ to $M$: $\bfx_i \gets \operatorname{Corrector}(\bfx_i)$, where the corrector is a score-based MCMC step (e.g.\ Langevin) targeting $p_{t_i}$.

nodes.name: Return final sample
nodes.statement: Return $\bfx_0$ as approximate draw from $p_0$.

nodes.name: PC sampler for VE SDE (Alg.~2)
nodes.statement: Specialization of the PC sampler for the VE SDE: predictor uses the reverse-diffusion update for VE; corrector is annealed Langevin dynamics with $\sigma_i$-conditioned scores.
nodes.pseudocode: $\bfx_N \sim \mcal{N}(\bfzero, \sM^2 \bfI)$; for $i = N-1$ down to $0$: $\bfx_i' \gets \bfx_{i+1} + (\sigma_{i+1}^2 - \sigma_i^2)\bfs_{\bftheta^*}(\bfx_{i+1}, \sigma_{i+1})$; $\bfz \sim \mcal{N}(\bfzero, \bfI)$; $\bfx_i \gets \bfx_i' + \sqrt{\sigma_{i+1}^2 - \sigma_i^2}\,\bfz$; for $j = 1$ to $M$: $\bfz \sim \mcal{N}(\bfzero, \bfI)$; $\bfx_i \gets \bfx_i + \epsilon_i \bfs_{\bftheta^*}(\bfx_i, \sigma_i) + \sqrt{2\epsilon_i}\,\bfz$; return $\bfx_0$.

nodes.name: Initialize $\bfx_N$ from $\mcal{N}(0, \sM^2 \bfI)$
nodes.statement: $\bfx_N \sim \mcal{N}(\bfzero, \sM^2 \bfI)$.

nodes.name: Reverse-diffusion predictor step (VE)
nodes.statement: $\bfx_i' \gets \bfx_{i+1} + (\sigma_{i+1}^2 - \sigma_i^2) \bfs_{\bftheta^*}(\bfx_{i+1}, \sigma_{i+1})$; then $\bfx_i \gets \bfx_i' + \sqrt{\sigma_{i+1}^2 - \sigma_i^2}\,\bfz$ with $\bfz \sim \mcal{N}(\bfzero, \bfI)$.

nodes.name: Langevin corrector inner loop (VE)
nodes.statement: For $j = 1, \ldots, M$: $\bfz \sim \mcal{N}(\bfzero, \bfI)$; $\bfx_i \gets \bfx_i + \epsilon_i \bfs_{\bftheta^*}(\bfx_i, \sigma_i) + \sqrt{2\epsilon_i}\,\bfz$.

nodes.name: Return $\bfx_0$
nodes.statement: Return $\bfx_0$.

nodes.name: PC sampler for VP SDE (Alg.~3)
nodes.statement: Specialization of the PC sampler for the VP SDE: predictor uses the reverse-diffusion update for VP; corrector is annealed Langevin dynamics with discrete-step-conditioned scores.
nodes.pseudocode: $\bfx_N \sim \mcal{N}(\bfzero, \bfI)$; for $i = N-1$ down to $0$: $\bfx_i' \gets (2 - \sqrt{1 - \beta_{i+1}})\bfx_{i+1} + \beta_{i+1} \bfs_{\bftheta^*}(\bfx_{i+1}, i+1)$; $\bfz \sim \mcal{N}(\bfzero, \bfI)$; $\bfx_i \gets \bfx_i' + \sqrt{\beta_{i+1}}\,\bfz$; for $j = 1$ to $M$: $\bfz \sim \mcal{N}(\bfzero, \bfI)$; $\bfx_i \gets \bfx_i + \epsilon_i \bfs_{\bftheta^*}(\bfx_i, i) + \sqrt{2\epsilon_i}\,\bfz$; return $\bfx_0$.

nodes.name: Initialize $\bfx_N \sim \mcal{N}(0, \bfI)$
nodes.statement: $\bfx_N \sim \mcal{N}(\bfzero, \bfI)$.

nodes.name: Reverse-diffusion predictor step (VP)
nodes.statement: $\bfx_i' \gets (2 - \sqrt{1 - \beta_{i+1}})\bfx_{i+1} + \beta_{i+1}\bfs_{\bftheta^*}(\bfx_{i+1}, i+1)$; then $\bfx_i \gets \bfx_i' + \sqrt{\beta_{i+1}}\,\bfz$.

nodes.name: Langevin corrector inner loop (VP)
nodes.statement: For $j = 1, \ldots, M$: $\bfz \sim \mcal{N}(\bfzero, \bfI)$; $\bfx_i \gets \bfx_i + \epsilon_i \bfs_{\bftheta^*}(\bfx_i, i) + \sqrt{2\epsilon_i}\,\bfz$.

nodes.name: Return $\bfx_0$
nodes.statement: Return $\bfx_0$.

nodes.name: Reverse diffusion sampler
nodes.statement: Discretize the reverse-time SDE in the same functional form as the forward discretization: $\bfx_i = \bfx_{i+1} - \bff_{i+1}(\bfx_{i+1}) + \bfG_{i+1}\bfG_{i+1}\tran \bfs_{\bftheta^*}(\bfx_{i+1}, i+1) + \bfG_{i+1}\bfz_{i+1}$.

nodes.name: Probability flow ODE sampler (deterministic)
nodes.statement: Numerically integrate the probability flow ODE backward from $\bfx_N \sim p_T$, e.g.\ via the iteration $\bfx_i = \bfx_{i+1} - \bff_{i+1}(\bfx_{i+1}) + \tfrac{1}{2}\bfG_{i+1}\bfG_{i+1}\tran \bfs_{\bftheta^*}(\bfx_{i+1}, i+1)$, or with a black-box ODE solver (RK45).
output: Optionally an exact log-likelihood via the instantaneous change-of-variables formula
nodes.pseudocode: Solve $\ud\bfx = [\bff(\bfx, t) - \tfrac{1}{2} g(t)^2 \bfs_{\bftheta^*}(\bfx, t)]\, \ud t$ from $t = T$ to $t = 0$ starting from $\bfx(T) \sim p_T$.

nodes.name: Ancestral sampler for SMLD models
nodes.statement: $\bfx_{i-1} = \bfx_i + (\sigma_i^2 - \sigma_{i-1}^2)\bfs_{\bftheta^*}(\bfx_i, i) + \sqrt{(\sigma_{i-1}^2(\sigma_i^2 - \sigma_{i-1}^2))/\sigma_i^2}\,\bfz_i$, derived by adapting the DDPM-style ancestral sampling rule to SMLD.

nodes.name: Imputation via reverse-time SDE on unknown dimensions
nodes.statement: Sample $\bomega(\bfx(0)) \mid \Omega(\bfx(0)) = \bfy$ by solving the reverse-time SDE for $\bfz(t) = \bomega(\bfx(t))$ with conditional score $\nabla_\bfz \log p_t([\bfz(t); \hat{\Omega}(\bfx(t))])$, where $\hat{\Omega}(\bfx(t)) \sim p_t(\Omega(\bfx(t)) \mid A)$.

nodes.name: Colorization via orthogonal-decoupled imputation
nodes.statement: Apply an orthogonal $3\times 3$ matrix $Q$ that maps RGB to a luminance channel plus two chroma channels; impute the chroma channels using AP231.7; transform back with $Q\tran$.
input: Gray-scale image (one channel of the orthogonally-decoupled space)

nodes.name: Time-dependent classifier-guided class-conditional sampling
nodes.statement: Train a time-dependent classifier $p_t(\bfy \mid \bfx(t))$ on noisy data, and sample from the conditional reverse-time SDE using $\nabla_\bfx \log p_t(\bfx \mid \bfy) = \bfs_{\bftheta^*}(\bfx, t) + \nabla_\bfx \log p_t(\bfy \mid \bfx)$.

nodes.name: Exact-likelihood computation via probability flow + Hutchinson
nodes.statement: Solve the probability flow ODE forward from $\bfx(0)$ to $\bfx(T)$ while accumulating $\int_0^T \nabla\cdot \tilde{\bff}_\bftheta(\bfx(t), t)\, \ud t$ using the Skilling-Hutchinson trace estimator; then $\log p_0(\bfx(0)) = \log p_T(\bfx(T)) + \int_0^T \nabla\cdot \tilde{\bff}_\bftheta(\bfx(t), t)\, \ud t$.

nodes.name: Annealed Langevin dynamics (corrector)
nodes.statement: Score-based MCMC corrector that updates $\bfx \gets \bfx + \epsilon\,\bfs_{\bftheta^*}(\bfx, \sigma_i) + \sqrt{2\epsilon}\,\bfz$ for $M$ steps per noise level, with step size $\epsilon = 2(r\,\norm{\bfz}_2/\norm{\bfs_{\bftheta^*}}_2)^2$ controlled by signal-to-noise ratio $r$.
input: Number of corrector steps $M$ per noise level
output: Updated sample $\bfx$ approximately distributed as $p_t$ at the current noise level

nodes.name: Annealed Langevin dynamics (Song & Ermon 2019)
nodes.statement: Run $M$ Langevin updates $\bfx_i^m = \bfx_i^{m-1} + \epsilon_i \bfs_{\bftheta^*}(\bfx_i^{m-1}, \sigma_i) + \sqrt{2\epsilon_i}\,\bfz_i^m$ at each noise scale $\sigma_i$ for $i = N, N-1, \ldots, 1$.

nodes.name: DDPM ancestral sampling
nodes.statement: $\bfx_{i-1} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-\beta_i}}(\bfx_i + \beta_i \bfs_{\bftheta^*}(\bfx_i, i)) + \sqrt{\beta_i}\,\bfz_i$ for $i = N, \ldots, 1$ starting from $\bfx_N \sim \mcal{N}(\bfzero, \bfI)$.

nodes.name: Score-based generative modeling via SDEs
nodes.statement: Given iid samples from an unknown data distribution $\pd$, learn to draw new samples by perturbing data with a forward SDE that ends at a tractable prior $p_T$, then simulating the corresponding reverse-time SDE driven by the time-dependent score $\nabla_\bfx \log p_t(\bfx)$.

nodes.name: Conditional / inverse-problem sampling with score models
nodes.statement: Given a forward likelihood $p(\bfy \mid \bfx)$, sample from the posterior $p_0(\bfx \mid \bfy)$ using only an unconditional score model $\bfs_{\bftheta^*}(\bfx, t) \approx \nabla_\bfx \log p_t(\bfx)$ plus an estimate of $\nabla_\bfx \log p_t(\bfy \mid \bfx(t))$.

nodes.name: Exact likelihood evaluation under a score-based model
nodes.statement: Compute exact $\log p_0(\bfx)$ for a score-based model defined by a forward SDE / probability flow ODE.

nodes.name: CIFAR-10 unconditional generation (FID 2.20, IS 9.89)
nodes.statement: NCSN++ cont. (deep, VE) trained with the continuous objective and PC sampling sets new state-of-the-art on $32\times 32$ CIFAR-10 unconditional generation, with Inception score $9.89$ and FID $2.20$.

nodes.name: CIFAR-10 likelihood (2.99 bits/dim)
nodes.statement: DDPM++ cont. (deep, sub-VP) achieves $2.99$ bits/dim on uniformly dequantized CIFAR-10, computed exactly via the probability flow ODE.

nodes.name: CelebA-HQ $1024\times 1024$ samples
nodes.statement: First high-fidelity $1024\times 1024$ images generated by a score-based model, trained on CelebA-HQ with a modified NCSN++ and the VE SDE using PC sampling at $2000$ steps.

nodes.name: Class-conditional CIFAR-10 generation
nodes.statement: Class-conditional samples from CIFAR-10 obtained by combining an unconditional NCSN++ score with a noise-conditional Wide-ResNet-28-10 classifier $p_t(\bfy \mid \bfx(t))$.

nodes.name: LSUN inpainting and colorization at $256\times 256$
nodes.statement: Inpainting and colorization on $256\times 256$ LSUN bedroom and church images using only an unconditional score-based model via the imputation algorithm AP231.7 / colorization algorithm AP231.8.

nodes.name: Empirical verification of unique identifiability
nodes.statement: Two independently-trained models (NCSN++ with 4 vs.\ 8 layers per resolution) trained with the VE SDE on CIFAR-10 produce nearly identical latent codes for the same input image, confirming the uniquely-identifiable encoding property of the probability flow ODE.

nodes.name: Latent-space interpolation and temperature rescaling on CelebA-HQ
nodes.statement: Spherical interpolations and temperature rescaling on $256\times 256$ CelebA-HQ latent codes obtained by integrating the VP probability flow ODE.

nodes.name: Equivalence of SMLD/DDPM weighting to inverse expected score-norm
nodes.statement: Both $\sigma_i^2$ in the SMLD objective and $(1-\alpha_i)$ in the DDPM objective satisfy $\propto 1/\mbb{E}[\norm{\nabla_\bfx \log p_{\sigma_i}(\tilde{\bfx}\mid\bfx)}_2^2]$, exposing SMLD and DDPM as the same weighted denoising score-matching family.

nodes.name: Tweedie denoising step at the end of sampling
nodes.statement: Because raw SDE samples carry residual noise that hurts FID, every reported sampler in this paper applies a single denoising step at $t = 0$ via Tweedie's formula.

nodes.name: Numerical $t = 0$ regularization
nodes.statement: Both VE and VP SDEs are integrated only on $t \in [\epsilon, 1]$ with $\epsilon = 10^{-5}$ (training, likelihood) or $\epsilon = 10^{-3}$ (VP sampling) to avoid singularities at $t = 0$.
